title: External reader sees the current state of every declared component on a public status page
asA: external reader visiting the status page without a login (customer, partner, or anonymous visitor)
iWant: a public page that lists every declared component and shows its current state from a fixed vocabulary
soThat: I answer 'is this service up right now' without opening a support ticket

acceptanceCriteria.description: The application serves the status page at a stable HTTP path declared in configuration (default /status), responds to an unauthenticated GET with 200 and text/html, and renders exactly the declared component list with no phantom components and no missing components.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the process is running with a component declaration that names N components
acceptanceCriteria.when: an unauthenticated GET is issued against the status page path
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response status code is 200, the Content-Type begins with text/html, and the rendered document contains exactly N component elements, each carrying the declared component name as text content

acceptanceCriteria.description: Each rendered component element carries its current state as a machine-readable attribute drawn from the fixed enum (operational, degraded, outage, maintenance); the attribute value is one of those four strings and no other.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the status page has been rendered with the declared components in mixed states
acceptanceCriteria.when: the rendered document is queried for the per-component state attribute
acceptanceCriteria.then: every component element carries a state attribute whose value is one of the four enum strings; no other value appears

acceptanceCriteria.description: The component render order on the page matches the declaration order in configuration; a component appearing at position K in the declaration renders at position K on the page.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the component declaration lists components in an order the operator has chosen
acceptanceCriteria.then: the rendered component elements appear in the same order as the declaration, verified by walking the rendered document's component elements top-to-bottom and comparing to the declared order
